title: Columbus's second voyage, 1493–96
summary: Seventeen ships and some 1,200 colonists out of Cádiz; a more southerly Atlantic run to Dominica and the Leeward Islands, Puerto Rico, the ruined Navidad and the new town of La Isabela; then Cuba and Jamaica, and home from Hispaniola by the Leewards.

events.label: Landfall at Dominica
events.text: Sighted on a Sunday, whence the name. This time Columbus came with seventeen ships and well over a thousand men, with horses, cattle, seed and sugar cane: not to look, but to found a colony.

events.label: La Isabela, the first European town in the New World
events.text: Founded on the north coast of Hispaniola and named for the queen. Fever, short rations and quarrels emptied it within a few years, and the Spanish moved to the south coast and built Santo Domingo. The ruins are in the Dominican Republic.
